I instructed Elena to hold 18 December for the 220/33 kV transformer technical specification, since it drives RFQ on 4 January and the M10 energisation date.

emails.subject: PEP Rev A - Project Director comments and approval for issue
emails.body:
Aziz,

I have reviewed the compiled PEP Rev A against the inputs from Mehmet (procurement and logistics, 4 Dec), Elena (engineering and design management, 4 Dec) and Sanjay (construction and site organisation, 4 Dec), and against your initial Risk Register (R-001 to R-018). The structure is sound and consistent with the Contract, the Kick-off minutes and the Level 1/Level 2 baseline. I approve PEP Rev A for internal issue today, subject to the comments below being closed in the same revision before it goes to QSE and Meridian.

Comments to close by 11 December:
1. Reporting and communication. Include the format agreed at the Kick-off Meeting exactly: monthly progress report with cut-off on the last day of the month and issue by the 5th (first report covers December 2026, due 5 January 2027), weekly look-ahead, one-page dashboard, Thursday weekly progress meeting, numbered letters under HEL001-L-DEPT-FROM-TO, email for coordination only, acknowledgement within 2 working days.
2. Review periods. State 10 working days for drawings, calculations and specifications, 14 days for plans and procedures, 5 working days for RFIs/TQs and 7 working days for method statements and ITPs. Mark deemed-approval wording as 'to be confirmed by Thomas Becker from the Contract' and do not paraphrase it. Elena plans on written approval or Code B/C only until then.
3. Critical items. The PEP must name the transformer (R-001, score 20, PO 12 Feb 2027 plus 36-40 weeks against M10 on 20 Jan 2028) and the A220 geotechnical/Basic Design review negative float (R-003, roughly 9-11 days against M04 on 15 Mar 2027) as the two items I will report on every week. Show the mitigation owner and date next to each.
4. M05 versus M07. Sanjay has flagged that mobilisation on 1 March 2027 falls before the construction permit on 20 March 2027. Add a controlled assumption: no works beyond camp, survey and track upgrade until Thomas and Shavkat Bobojonov confirm in writing what is permitted before the permit. Remove any wording that implies piling or civil works earlier.
5. NTP preconditions. Show the APG and Performance Security route (QSE comments due 7 Dec, bank acceptance 9 Dec, signatory pack 11 Dec, advance payment M03 on 5 Jan 2027) and land allocation A110 (QSE written status due 10 Dec) as external dependencies, not HEP-controlled dates.
6. Specification dates. Include Mehmet's RFQ dates (21 Dec for modules, 4 Jan for transformer) and Elena's specification dates (18 Dec transformer, 31 Dec for P02/P03) in one table so the dependency is visible to the reader.
7. Authority matrix. Approvals by me: letters to QSE, payment applications, change orders, monthly report. Contract notices go through Thomas Becker for review before my signature.

On your request in the 5 December risk email: I confirm the Level 1 summary and the reporting calendar can follow tomorrow, 8 December. Please send them to me and Priya for a cross-check against the PEP text before they are attached. My comments on the Risk Register are covered by items 3, 4 and 6; I will not hold up the register for anything else.

Plan: revised PEP Rev A to me by 11 December, Nilufar to log it in 1/03, my final sign-off 14 December, formal submission to QSE and Meridian by 15 December as agreed (ACT-002-KOM-07). QSE and OWE have 14 days from receipt, so I expect comments around 29 December and will plan the holiday period accordingly. I do not want any surprises on that date, so if any input is going to slip, tell me today, not on the 14th.

Regards,
Rajan Iyer
Project Director, HEP

emails.subject: 220/33 kV transformer technical specification required by 18 December
emails.body:
Elena,

Mehmet has flagged the 220/33 kV transformer as the main schedule risk on the project, and I agree with him. It is R-001 in Aziz's register (score 20). With a 36-40 week manufacturing lead time, a PO on 12 February 2027 gives delivery between 15 November and 15 December 2027. That leaves about five weeks at best before M10 plant substation energisation on 20 January 2028 for installation, testing and commissioning. Every day lost on the specification is a day lost on M10, and we cannot recover it by hurrying the factory.

Please hold 18 December 2026 for the issued technical specification for the 220/33 kV power transformer. This is an instruction, not a target. Mehmet needs it to issue the RFQ on 4 January 2027 and award on 12 February 2027, and the QSE and Meridian vendor approval step has to fit inside that window.

What I need from you:
1. Confirm by Wednesday 9 December that 18 December is secure, and name who is writing it. If you need input from Sergey Volkov (GridWorks) on the 220 kV interface, from UzGridCo through Thomas on the grid code and protection requirements, or from Aziz on the single line diagram, tell me today so I can chase them myself.
2. Issue the specification in a form that can go straight to RFQ: rating, vector group, tap changer range, impedance, losses evaluation, cooling, bushings and cable boxes, tests, FAT, transport and delivery to site. Where a value depends on the Basic Design or on the grid operator, state the assumption and the range, and do not wait for the final number. A conditional specification on 18 December is better than a perfect one in January.
3. Send it to Meridian for early review under the 10 working day period at the same time as it goes to Mehmet, so that approval does not start after the RFQ. If Sophie Laurent can give a faster review for this one item, I will ask Khalid.
4. Hold 31 December for the P02 and P03 specifications as already planned, and tell me now if both dates cannot be met by the same team.

If the 18 December date cannot be held, I want to hear it by 9 December with the reason and the earliest realistic date, and I will take it up myself. Mehmet and Aziz are copied so the RFQ and risk register stay aligned.

Regards,
Rajan Iyer
Project Director, HEP
